overview: Black develops the queen's knight before the e- or d-pawn, aiming for a Two Knights Tango. After 3.Nf3 e6 4.Nc3 Bb4 or 3.Nf3 d6 Black builds a solid set-up, and 3.d5 Ne5 gains time for Black. White takes space with d4/c4 and e4 or e3, and Black uses the knight on c6 to pressure d4 and e5.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with Nc3, e4 or e3 and play for space with the c4/d4 pawns.
Meet ...e5 with d5 and gain time against the c6 knight.

black_ideas.idea: Develop into Nimzo or other Indian set-ups with the knight on c6, then ...e5 or ...Bb4.
Provoke d5 and attack with ...Ne5 or ...Nb4 ideas.

typical_structures.structure: Indian-style centre with White pawns on c4/d4 and Black pieces pressuring the centre.

character.notes: Strategic Indian-style play with no forced sacrifices; White typically has more space.

soundness.notes: Sound for Black though a little passive for the knight on c6.

structure.notes: Centre not fixed; normal d4/c4 versus ...e6/...d6 possibilities.

approach.notes: A sideline that strong players seldom use, mostly for surprise.

level.notes: Fewer main lines to memorise but Indian structures need understanding.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.d5 Ne5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 Nc6 3. d5 Ne5
sublines_that_differ.how: White chases the knight and Black gets the e5 outpost; very different structures.

character.reason: Quiet development with no forcing play and no fortress.

soundness.reason: A playable Indian set-up though a little passive.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided with various Indian set-ups available.

approach.reason: Rarely chosen by strong players, used for surprise.

level.reason: Not much theory but Indian structures need understanding.

plans.reason: Black lets White build a centre and pressures it with pieces.
